minutes.headline: Commission accepted pumping invoices to extend a grease-trap permit; no vote on an external trap for Bad Larry's, revisited Oct 10.
minutes.summary: The Sewer Commission held a Zoom meeting with heavy audio and quorum problems. It extended the reboot restaurant's grease interceptor permit on invoices alone, and discussed at length the recent grease clog traced to the Bad Larry's area, agreeing informally that an external trap is needed but taking no vote. It also approved prior minutes and appointed the business manager enforcing agent for non-criminal disposition of delinquent bills, and heard the business manager's report on technicians, jetting, and job classification.

public_comment.topic: Chair asked for public comment; none offered.
Final public comment requested; none offered.

votes.motion: Extend/issue the reboot restaurant's permit on the invoices as evidence of pumping, expecting a full report next cycle; amended to condition issuance on receipt of invoices
votes.outcome: passed (roll call, four yes votes heard)

votes.motion: Appoint Ms. Bertram as enforcing agent for non-criminal disposition

budget_items.what_was_said: The restaurant owner said pumping the large tank is costly, making an early extra pumping a hardship.
A commissioner noted clearing the clog and the last jetting were very expensive for a tight Sewer Commission budget.
Extra flow charged by Leominster during the storm cost a little over a stated amount, included in the DPW's request.
First-quarter bills have a high delinquency rate, with some unpaid for over a year; non-criminal disposition ticketing is being pursued.
The business manager recommended increasing the jetting line item next year since recommended jetting was not being met.
Committee scores for the business manager and assistant positions were compared with staff's own ratings.
Bad Larry's owner cited sums spent on blockages and an external trap that would be the landlord's cost.

decisions.decision: No vote on an external grease trap for Bad Larry's; the business manager will draft a letter stressing the seriousness to the landlord and owner, inviting them to the Oct 10 meeting.
Bad Larry's permit is not revoked and the establishment may continue operating until the next meeting.
Business manager to invite the new CTE technician and the CTE business manager to a commission meeting.
Business manager position rating to remain on the agenda/report; Ms. Bertram to send the rating scale.
Staff to also contact the pumping company directly for the missing reports.

what_happened.line: The Commission extended the reboot restaurant's grease interceptor permit on pumping invoices as evidence, in a roll-call vote with four yes votes heard.
The Commission took no vote on an external grease trap for Bad Larry's and did not revoke its permit; the business manager will write the landlord and owner.
Bad Larry's may keep operating until the next meeting, and the owner and landlord are invited to the Oct 10 meeting.
The Commission appointed the business manager as enforcing agent for non-criminal disposition of delinquent sewer bills, in a roll call with three yes votes.
The business manager reported that first-quarter sewer bills have a high delinquency rate and that recommended jetting was not being met.

why_it_matters: Grease clogs in the sewer line are costly to clear and fall on a tight Sewer Commission budget, so the unsettled question of who pays for an external trap at Bad Larry's bears on sewer costs.
Ticketing delinquent sewer bills is now possible, which affects residents with unpaid accounts and the revenue that funds the system.
watch_next: Oct 10 Sewer Commission meeting: the Bad Larry's permit and external trap are expected back, with the owner and landlord invited.
The business manager's letter to the landlord and owner, and the missing pumping reports for the reboot restaurant, due by the next cycle.
